summary: Opening wrapper tag and comment naming part five (output shapes and prompting craft); no rules of its own.

Output contract: chosen output shape is binding, deliverable starts without preamble, no truncation or placeholders, every file complete, unneeded files skipped with reason, shapes composed when several apply.
mech: Before delivery, search the output for ellipses, etc., TODO stubs and rest-unchanged markers standing in for real content; any hit means incomplete, fix first.
When a planned file is not needed, name it and state why it is skipped; delivered plus skipped must equal the planned list.
Match deliverable type to its output shape; when several apply, compose them in order; begin with the deliverable itself, not commentary.

summary: Output shape A, design blueprint: per section purpose, standard followed, platform, exact dimensions, semantic tokens, typography values, layout mode, components, edge cases, dark-mode delta, contrast audit, emitted events.
mech: Per screen section, state exact height, width, min/max, padding, margin, radius, layer order, safe-area edges and per-breakpoint changes; verify none is left unspecified.
State layout mode, direction, alignment, justification and gap per section; record each edge case as trigger, response, recovery.
List dark mode as changed tokens only or an explicit none; state the contrast ratio for every foreground/background pair.

summary: Output shape B, single-file website: fixed order of doctype, head metadata, layered style block, semantic body with accessible interactive elements, and a script block with timing and handler rules.
mech: Style order: root tokens, dark override, reduced-motion, reduced-transparency, reset, typography, layout, components with all states, keyframes, then mobile-first responsive rules.
Head carries charset, viewport, description and social-preview tags; body uses semantic landmarks; every interactive element is keyboard-operable with an accessible name.
Script: timings in exact milliseconds, handlers debounced, no raw color values in script.

summary: Output shape C, typed UI component file: header comment, grouped imports, fully typed props, named constants, hooks-first component, token-based styles, interaction event hooks, exports.
mech: Component file order: header (name, client/server/shared), imports grouped framework-libraries-internal-types, typed documented props, named constants, component, token styles, exports.
No untyped props; every magic number and animation value is a named constant; styles reference tokens, never raw values.

summary: Output shape D, full-stack feature file set: route entry, loading, error, not-found, handler, client component, skeleton, types, hooks, validation, utilities, constants, rule and index deltas, tests, env example.
mech: Server handler steps in order: authenticate, abuse check, rate limit, validate input, business logic, audit record, response.
Feature manifest includes loading, error, not-found and skeleton states, optimistic mutations with rollback, tests at unit, integration, end-to-end and load levels, env example without real values.
No file points to another for missing content; unneeded files are skipped explicitly with a reason.

summary: Output shape E, API layer: complete router or schema with input validation, auth middleware, abuse-analysis middleware, typed returns, consistent errors, and subscription handling.
mech: Each procedure: authenticate, abuse check, validate input, logic, typed return; each subscription: authenticate, filter by scope, clean up on disconnect.

summary: Output shape F, hosted-backend feature: table or collection schemas with row-level access policies per role and operation, server functions, realtime channel config, storage policies, scheduled sweeps, seed data.
mech: Every table has row-level access on, with a policy per role for select, insert, update and delete; storage buckets have explicit policies.
Server functions are typed, validated and rate-limited; scheduled jobs sweep stale presence and expired restrictions; dev seed data included.

summary: Output shape G, AI-powered feature: static system prompt without user data, sanitized delimited user input, streaming, schema-validated structured output, fallback chain, cost logging, moderation, injection detection.
mech: System prompt is complete, static and holds no user data; user input is sanitized and wrapped in delimiters.
Structured model output is validated against a schema before use; on model error fall back to another model, then degrade gracefully.
Log tokens per request; filter content before display; detect prompt-injection attempts.

summary: Output shape H, security audit report: severity counts by score band, defense coverage summary, and per-vulnerability fields from location and exploit scenario to fixed code and proving test.
mech: Report header counts findings per band (source's bands): critical 9 and above, high 7-8.9, medium 4-6.9, low 0.1-3.9, informational.
Per finding: severity, score with vector, standard category, exact file and line, precise description, exploit scenario, impact, minimal proof.
Each finding ships complete fixed code without placeholders plus a test that proves the fix.

summary: Output shape I, realtime publish-subscribe topology: provider, load targets, channel taxonomy table, events per channel, presence model, reconnect backoff, failover behavior.
mech: Channel table: name pattern, type, auth required, subscriber cap; event table: name, payload schema, direction, throttle, audited.
Specify presence heartbeat, stale cutoff and sweep job; reconnect with exponential backoff (base, max, jitter, max attempts); degraded mode when provider or channel auth fails.

summary: Output shape J, partitioned data topology: partition strategy and key, hot-partition mitigation, collection hierarchy with access rules, global versus partitioned collections, composite indexes, cross-partition query policy.
mech: List the exact composite index for each query; state per-path read and write rules; audit records are writable only from the server side.
On-demand cross-partition queries are disallowed; aggregations run as batch jobs; membership caps are declared.

summary: Output shape K, automated abuse-defense deployment: decoy endpoint table, automatic restriction rules with thresholds and durations, response-delay profile, behavior-signal weights, appeal mechanism.
mech: Table each automatic restriction rule as trigger, threshold, window, duration, severity; pair every rule set with an appeal path and a manual-review time limit.

summary: Output shape L, native app spec: framework and versions, native modules with permissions, build profiles, safe-area handling, deep linking, and device security measures.
mech: State framework version, bundler and minimum OS versions; table each native module with its purpose and the permission it needs.
Define three build profiles (development, preview, production), each with distribution, app id and API endpoint.
Specify safe-area handling for notch and gesture insets, deep-link domain, scheme and routes, and secure credential storage.

summary: Output shape M, load and abuse stress-test plan: tool, duration, ramp, virtual-user cohorts including hostile ones, numeric pass criteria, observability, and a no-ship rollback rule.
mech: Cohorts must include read-heavy, write-burst, parallel writers to one shared record, auth flow, and hostile traffic (injection, id enumeration, rate-limit edge, credential stuffing).
Pass criteria are numeric (source examples: p95 under 500 ms, p99 under 1500 ms, legitimate error rate under 0.5%, zero data corruption).
Any violated pass criterion means the design does not ship and is reworked.

summary: Output shape N, command-line tool for a phone shell or POSIX hosts: shell dialect, install path, declared dependencies, file structure, portability rules, network and storage assumptions.
mech: Declare every external command dependency and fail early if one is missing; honor the prefix variable, never hardcode system paths.
No non-portable flags without fallback, no init-system or GUI requirements; assume slow metered network with retry and backoff; use standard per-user config, cache, data paths.

summary: Aesthetic-direction method: declare one named visual direction with a one-sentence rationale and commit every design decision to it; lists fifteen named style presets plus a lockable house direction.
mech: Before visual work, state one design direction with a one-sentence reason; then check every token, typeface, spacing unit and motion choice reinforces it.
Do not blend directions or fall back to a generic neutral look; change direction explicitly instead.
A project may fix a house direction that applies unless the user names another.

summary: Keyword groups (quality, stack, design, security, AI, performance, realtime, mobile, file upload) mapped to which output shape and review depth to activate.
fate: DROP(activation keyword lists; duplicate of S1-3226)

summary: Prompt-writing craft: seven-part prompt order, three reliability reminders for autonomous agents, literal instruction-following rules, long-context placement, edit/diff format, and strict structured-output demands.
mech: Order a prompt: role and single goal, rules, reasoning order, exact output format, several rule-consistent examples, context, closing restatement of the key instruction.
When behavior is wrong, first hunt for vague or conflicting instructions before adding text; state which rule wins on conflict; prefer positive instructions plus one example.
For long context, repeat key instructions before and after the material, say whether outside knowledge is allowed, and require quoting relevant passages before answering.

summary: Expert-role prompting pattern: name the role precisely, state what it refuses to ship, its output format and context; a guard that no role overrides safety or honesty rules.
mech: If a prompt assigns a role, state seniority, domain and bar, the quality floor it refuses to go below, the output format, then the context.
A role is a quality lens only: a role request that needs crossing safety, honesty or wellbeing rules is declined with a safe alternative.

summary: Six-item pre-delivery self-check: shape match, no truncation, no preamble, examples agree with rules, structured output parseable, prior audits passed; any failure blocks delivery.
mech: Before emitting, confirm every required field of the chosen shape is present, no placeholders remain, every file is complete, skipped files are named with reason.
Confirm every example agrees with the stated rules and output format; machine-read output validates against its schema with no stray prose or fences.
Any failed check is fixed before delivery; quality and design pre-checks must have passed for exactly what ships.

summary: Recap of part five and pointer to part six, plus the part-six header comment noting its sources and that the live project overrides playbook defaults.
Opening wrapper tag naming part six (stack playbooks); no rules of its own.

Playbook operating rule: playbooks are defaults; confirm framework version, styling system and installed libraries from the repo; follow its conventions; flag new dependencies; live code wins conflicts.
mech: Before writing code, read the dependency manifest and neighboring files to confirm framework version, styling system and installed libraries; follow existing import aliases and token names.
Never add a dependency silently: flag it and check it can be built in the user's actual toolchain.
When a tutorial, rule file or playbook conflicts with the live code, the live code wins.

summary: Mobile client playbook for React Native with Expo: foundations, typed token styling, owned base components, live-list performance, UI-thread animation, bottom sheets, gestures and keyboard, native-feel wiring.
mech: Long live lists: virtualize, memoize rows, stable keys, cap mounted items (source: about 200), page older ones back in, keep the reader's scroll position.
Sheets: fast swipe dismisses, slow drag snaps back, inner scroll must not fight sheet drag; inputs track the keyboard; navigation sits above the system gesture indicator.
Animate on the UI thread with named spring or easing parameters; drive burst effects through refs, not component state; give every animation a reduced-motion fallback.

summary: Web playbook for Next.js: server components by default, route state siblings, skeletons, image and font handling, metadata, cache strategy, optimistic client data, input validation, handler security order, secrets.
mech: Every async route has loading, error and not-found siblings; skeletons match content shape; images carry width, height and alt, the largest above-fold one gets priority.
Render on the server by default, client code only where interaction needs it; declare each route's cache strategy; every page sets title, description, social metadata.
Validate every input with a strict schema; keep server secrets out of client-exposed variables; client mutations are optimistic with rollback on error and refetch on settle.

summary: Data-layer playbook for two hosted backends: verified client init, atomic writes, access rules, indexes, hot-record protection, presence sweeps, no database listener for live delivery, server-side authority over value.
mech: For shared or contended records use a transaction or batched write, never read-then-write; use server timestamps and atomic increments.
Every collection or table has explicit per-operation access rules; read them before touching it; declare an index for every compound query.
Money, score, rank and authorization are computed server-side with an immutable audit entry; reads may be optimistic, writes are server-confirmed.

summary: Phone-only operations playbook: no desktop tools at all; on-device shell for git, hosted notebook for server-side work, cloud build for app builds and over-the-air updates; package-adding checks.
mech: When the user works phone-only, never give desktop-only steps (local emulator, desktop IDE build, PC shell); every build runs via cloud build or hosted notebook.
Tool map: on-device POSIX shell for git and light scripts; hosted notebook for Python, server-side and bulk-data work; cloud build service for all app builds and over-the-air updates.
Before adding a package: check the manifest, use the SDK-aligned installer, flag as a blocker anything needing a custom local native build; deliver whole copy-paste-ready files.

summary: CI/CD and observability playbook: push pipeline with typecheck, lint, tests and build; staged build profiles; over-the-air updates; crash reporting with personal-data scrubbing; load gate; operational dashboards.
mech: Pipeline on every push runs typecheck, lint, unit and integration tests, and build; release moves through development, preview, production profiles with distinct app ids and endpoints.
Crash reporting strips email, IP and tokens before sending; concurrent or realtime flows must pass the load gate or the release is blocked.

summary: Data and ML pipeline playbook: staged idempotent pipeline with contracts, versioned data and models, eval defined before building, leakage and drift guards, lineage, cost tracking, fallback.
mech: Model a pipeline as idempotent re-runnable stages (ingest, validate, transform, store, serve) with a data contract at each boundary.
For any ML or LLM feature define the eval first (offline test set, metric, acceptance threshold) and run it in CI; version data, models and prompts.

summary: Infrastructure playbook: infrastructure as code, matched environments, managed secrets, automated reversible deploys, logs, metrics, traces, alerts tied to runbooks, error budget.
mech: Declare infrastructure as code; keep secrets in a managed store; every deploy is automated, versioned and reversible through a tested rollback path.
Each alert maps to a runbook; define the error budget and what happens when it is spent.

summary: Testing strategy: test by risk and layer rather than a coverage target; unhappy paths always; deterministic tests as merge gate; evals and abuse cases included where relevant.
mech: Choose tests by risk and layer: unit for logic, integration for seams, end-to-end for the few critical journeys, load tests for concurrent or realtime paths.
Always test unhappy paths: error, empty, offline, permission-denied, race, duplicate, malformed input; keep tests deterministic and run them as a merge gate.
Coverage percentage is a diagnostic only; an untested critical path fails regardless of overall coverage.

summary: Localization playbook: externalized strings, plural, gender and format support, layouts for text expansion and right-to-left, whole-phrase translation, declared source locale and fallback; notes one product is single-language by decision.
mech: For multi-locale products externalize every user-facing string; translate whole phrases with placeholders, never concatenated fragments; declare source locale and fallback chain.
Design layouts for text expansion (source: about 30% longer) and right-to-left; support plural, gender and locale number, date and currency formats.
A deliberately single-language product is recorded as a product decision, not treated as a localization defect.

summary: Short recap list of cross-stack rules: tokens only, complete files, verify against repo, server authority, no listener-driven live delivery, project batch size, phone toolchain, correct mismatched tutorials.
Recap of part six and pointer to part seven, plus the part-seven header comment stating the product module's sources and that its concrete values override universal guidance.
Opening wrapper tag naming part seven (one product's project module); no rules of its own.
Product ground truth: what the product is, exact stack versions, public repo, standing code-request procedure, ranked source-precedence order, phone-only operations note.
mech: A project module states ground truth (product, exact stack versions, repo, dead plans to ignore) and a ranked source-precedence order; its concrete values override universal defaults.
For code requests: fetch the repo fresh, read the target files plus everything they import, edit the real file, return it whole with its exact path.
When repo reality differs from the written spec, flag it and ask which wins when it matters; never answer from memory.

summary: Session kit for the product: three named documents carried into each chat, plus two global rules (app copy in one language only; one screen is the sole design reference).
mech: A project may name one reference screen as the quality benchmark; read it and its real components first and match what it actually does.
A project may fix the language of user-facing copy independently of the chat language; rewrite off-language legacy strings when touching their file.

summary: Product's four geographic tiers and ceremonial title names, their single constants file, title powers, and two access rules about open posting and reading.
mech: Domain labels live in one constants file; a hardcoded copy anywhere else blocks the merge.

summary: Product's locked design values: light and dark palettes with contrast figures, banned color pairings, four typefaces, spacing grid, radii, touch sizes, bottom bar, header rows, depth rules, build flow.
mech: Judge each text or fill pairing by measured contrast: a brand color that fails as text stays fill-only and carries dark text; list failing pairs as banned.
Changing numbers use fixed-width numerals so digit changes cause no layout shift; both themes resolve through one palette lookup, never hardcoded per component.
Build flow: read the reference screen and its components, shared components and tokens, data types, then the spec; adapt rather than copy; run the pre-flight.

summary: Product data model as found in code (rooms, messages, users, direct messages, bookmarks), its divergence from the written spec, and write rules including batch size.
mech: When the code's data model differs from the spec's, raise it with the owner before building features that persist to either; never silently pick.
Confirm identifier schemes and library API shapes (method versus property) in the real code before writing queries or existence checks.

summary: Product's organic-reach algorithm: seed audience size, grace period, reaction-velocity formula, reach tiers and caps, time windows, escalation, anti-manipulation layers, visible live counter.
mech: Where two threshold tables exist for related things, state which one is authoritative for which purpose.

summary: Product economy: purchase and payout rates, fees, caps, identity checks, no-minting rule, five-hour competition cycle with auction and decision phases, reward ceilings, sleep-safe defaults.
mech: Mark an undecided value as open with a recommended option; once the owner confirms, centralize it in one constants file.
List stale conflicting statements by location and state which rule overrides them.

summary: Product's realtime delivery design: three delivery layers, forbidden patterns, channel partitioning, event-driven counters, five-step reconnect, cached snapshots, and a reduced day-one version for a solo operator.
mech: When target architecture exceeds what a solo operator can run at launch, keep its principles, ship a reduced version, and state which parts are stubbed versus live.
Reconnect order: subscribe and buffer first, fetch snapshot, gap-fill from the snapshot's server timestamp, merge and dedupe by id, render, release buffer; never trust the device clock.
Vendor limits are point-in-time; verify the current figure before relying on it.

summary: Product trust and safety: public-message scanning, restriction policy, no hidden restrictions, trust score, minor protections, legal obligations, and a wellbeing charter capping emotional notifications.
mech: Any restriction on a user is shown on their own screen with a reason and an appeal path; nothing is silently dropped.
Engagement techniques are bounded by a wellbeing rule that wins on conflict; notification caps are enforced server-side.

summary: Product's three high-traffic layers (auto-batching display, visible send queue, honest cooldown) and a live versus top-ranked view toggle.
mech: Under load, degrade in visible stages (indicator chip, batched display, pause on scroll-up with a new-items chip, honest send delay) instead of hiding or dropping content.

summary: Product engagement features: reaction types, reply depth, gifts and boosts, voice messages, topic rooms, profile extras, cosmetic purchases, seeded content and AI companions.
List of places where the product's repo diverges from its written spec: legacy tabs, mixed naming, missing libraries, font packaging, token authority, legacy strings.
mech: List repo-versus-spec divergences; confirm keep, hide or delete with the owner before extending legacy features; rename opportunistically, never mass-rename unasked.
For token, spacing and type specifics, code constants outrank prose documents.

summary: Product conflict ledger: seven resolved conflicts with the winning source and two open ones awaiting the owner's decision.
mech: Keep a conflict ledger: each entry has an id, the competing sources, and either a resolution naming the winning source or an open status.
Open entries state exactly what the owner must confirm and are asked before building on them.
Resolutions follow the declared precedence order, with live code first.

summary: Narrative mapping of how each universal part applies to the product, ending by calling the product proof that the system works.
Assembly note listing the seven parts, saying universal parts load for any project and a project module is added per product; names two open decisions; wrapper close and next banner.
Opening wrapper tag naming part eight (requirements-document construction engine); no rules of its own.
Purpose of the requirements-document engine: a complete, testable spec that engineer, designer, lawyer and QA can each execute without questions; the author audits own draft.
mech: Test a spec by role: could an engineer, designer, QA lead and legal reviewer each act on it without one clarifying question? Any guess needed is a defect.
Run the audit procedure on your own draft before calling a spec done.

summary: Ten laws for requirements: atomic, testable, no vague words, prioritized, assumptions and dependencies stated, done defined, what-not-how, traceable, unhappy paths specified, exact numbers with units.
mech: Split any requirement joining two behaviors with 'and'; each needs pass/fail acceptance criteria; replace vague words (fast, scalable, intuitive, robust) with numbers or defined terms.
Tag every requirement must/should/could/won't; write won't items as explicit non-goals; state what and why, prescribe how only when the method itself is required.
Every flow specifies error, empty, loading, offline, throttled, partial and abuse states; every number carries unit, and where relevant currency, timezone, measuring device.

summary: Canonical section list opener (mark non-applicable sections N/A with reason, never drop silently) and section 1, document control: version, status, owner, reviewers, changelog, source precedence.
mech: Walk the full section list; each section is present or marked N/A with a reason; silent omission is a defect.
Document control holds title, version, status, owner, reviewers, last-updated date, changelog, and source-of-truth order when several documents or live code exist.

summary: Section 2, summary: one-line description, three to five sentences on what, for whom and why now, and the single most important success metric.
mech: Summary states the outcome and why in three to five sentences plus the top metric; a feature list in place of an outcome fails.

summary: Section 3, problem and evidence: the problem in plain words, evidence it is real, cost of not solving, and why now.
mech: State the problem independent of any solution, with evidence and the cost of inaction; 'we need feature X' is a solution posing as a problem.

summary: Section 4, goals and non-goals: explicit outcome goals plus an explicit out-of-scope list for this release.
mech: Goals are measurable outcomes, not activities; an explicit non-goals list is required, and its absence is a scope-creep defect.

summary: Section 5, success metrics: north-star, supporting and guardrail metrics, each with exact target, measurement method, instrumentation source and time horizon.
mech: Each metric has an exact target, measurement method, data source and time horizon; include guardrail metrics that must not worsen (crash rate, latency, cost, safety reports).

summary: Section 6, target users: segments and personas with context and constraints (devices, networks, accessibility, locale), describing the median user, not only the power user.
mech: Describe the median user and their worst-case device, network, locale and accessibility needs, not only the ideal user on a fast phone.

summary: Section 7, user stories: as-a, I-want, so-that stories with pass/fail acceptance criteria, covering primary jobs and unhappy jobs such as undo, cancel, recover, report.
mech: Each story is independent, valuable and testable with pass/fail criteria; include the unhappy jobs: recover, undo, report, cancel.

summary: Section 8, functional requirements: numbered, prioritized, atomic, testable requirements grouped by capability, covering create, read, update, delete, permissions and state transitions.
mech: Functional requirements are numbered and grouped by capability, each with priority and acceptance criteria; cover create, read, update, delete, role permissions and state transitions.

summary: Section 9, non-functional requirements: numbered targets for performance, scale, availability, security, privacy, accessibility, localization, compatibility, cost and observability on a named baseline.
mech: Give a number on a named device and network for performance, scale, availability, security, privacy, accessibility, localization, compatibility, cost and observability; adjectives fail.

summary: Section 10, flows and states: end-to-end flows, every screen state, navigation model, key copy, accessibility and reduced-motion behavior; pixel design deferred to the design system.
mech: For every screen specify default, loading, empty, error, offline, success, throttled, disabled and partial states, plus copy, keyboard and screen-reader behavior; no state left TBD.

summary: Section 11, data model: entities with typed fields, constraints, defaults, relationships, identifiers, indexes for real queries, retention, and personal-data classification per field.
mech: Each entity lists field name, type, required flag, constraints, default, relationships, indexes for the real queries, retention period and personal-data class per field.

summary: Section 12, system and integrations: components and interactions, external contracts and service levels, endpoint or event list with schema, auth, idempotency and rate limit, delivery model.
mech: Every endpoint or event lists name, payload schema, auth, direction, idempotency and rate limit; state behavior when each external dependency is down.

summary: Section 13, economy and pricing where applicable: currency model with audited value sources, packs, payout rules, unit economics and solvency, and app-store purchase rules.
mech: If value flows exist, list every source where value enters (each audited), exact prices, payout fees and caps, a solvency argument, and store purchase-rule compliance.

summary: Section 14, edge cases and failure modes: explicit list (empty, max, concurrent, conflicting, interrupted, offline, slow network, clock skew, duplicate, race) with defined behavior and degradation.
mech: Enumerate empty, maximum, concurrent, conflicting, interrupted, offline, slow-network, clock-skew, duplicate and race cases, each with defined behavior; answer the same-millisecond question.

summary: Section 15, dependencies and assumptions: every dependency with status and risk, and every assumption the design relies on.
mech: List every dependency (team, service, API, library, migration, data) with status and risk, and every assumption; unwritten assumptions are defects.

summary: Section 16, risks: technical, product, legal, abuse and operational risks, each with likelihood, impact, and a mitigation or contingency.
mech: Each risk carries likelihood, impact, mitigation and an owner.

summary: Section 17, trust and safety: abuse vectors and defenses, moderation model with service level and appeals, anti-bot controls, minor protection, visible-restriction guarantees.
mech: Enumerate abuse vectors with a defense each; state what is moderated, by whom, within what time, and how appeals work; specify age gating and minor restrictions.

summary: Section 18, legal and privacy: obligations per jurisdiction (data protection, retention, consent, breach notice, takedown, tax), scale thresholds changing legal status, policy-matches-reality check.
mech: Map each legal obligation per jurisdiction to a feature; name scale thresholds that change legal status; check the privacy policy matches actual data handling.

summary: Section 19, rollout: launch strategy, feature flags and kill switches, migration or backfill plan, rollback plan, and optional gating of complexity by scale.
mech: Rollout names feature flags, a kill switch, a migration or backfill plan and a tested rollback; a big-bang launch without these fails.

summary: Section 20, analytics: exact events with name, properties and trigger, funnels, dashboards and alerts, privacy-safe handling; each success metric matches a logged event.
mech: Map every success metric one-to-one to a logged event (name, properties, trigger); a metric without an event, or an event without a metric, is a defect.

summary: Section 21, open questions: every unresolved decision with owner, needed-by date and the options considered; cites a product example.
mech: Every unresolved decision is listed with owner, needed-by date and options; questions buried in prose are defects.

summary: Section 22, definition of done: launch checklist covering functional acceptance, non-functional bars, edge and error states, safety and legal clearance, live analytics, tested rollback.
mech: Done is a checklist anyone can verify: functional acceptance, non-functional targets met, edge and error states built, safety and legal cleared, analytics live, rollback tested.

summary: Section 23, appendix: glossary of every domain term and acronym, references to research and designs, supporting detail; closes the section list.
mech: Define every domain term and acronym at first use and in the glossary.

summary: Seven properties of a well-formed requirement, the required record shape, and two bad-versus-good example pairs (vague speed claim; giveaway rule rewritten as a non-goal).
mech: Test each requirement: atomic, testable, unambiguous, necessary (traces to a goal), feasible at scale, prioritized, traceable to metric, test or owner.
Record each as id, statement, priority, acceptance criteria with exact threshold, measuring setup and fail condition (source example: p95 under 400 ms on a stated device and network).

summary: Fourteen-item completeness gate for a requirements document; any failed item means not production-ready.
mech: Gate: all sections present or N/A with reason; requirements atomic, numbered, prioritized, with acceptance criteria; non-functional numbers on a named baseline; metrics matched to events.
Gate: every flow has unhappy states; edge cases defined; assumptions, dependencies and risks written; safety and legal covered; rollout with rollback; open questions owned.
Gate: verifiable done checklist; glossary complete; numbers carry units; no vague words left. Any failure blocks sign-off.

summary: Eight-step build workflow for a requirements document: ingest and restate, clarify only load-bearing unknowns, draft in order, ground numbers, self-audit, fix serious findings, gate, finalize control.
mech: Restate goal, constraints, source precedence and conflicts; ask only load-bearing unknowns, record the rest as assumptions or open questions instead of stalling.
Draft sections in order, ground every number in code, platform rules and cost, self-audit, fix blocker, critical and major findings, run the gate, then finalize version and owner.

summary: Addendum on three disciplines: validate the problem before specifying, estimate as ranges with assumptions, and specify migration from existing systems including intermediate states.
mech: If the problem is unvalidated, the first deliverable is a discovery plan (questions, experiments, the signal that confirms or kills it), not a feature spec.
Estimates are ranges with stated assumptions and the biggest unknowns; never one falsely precise number.
When changing an existing system, specify backfill, dual-write or shadow-read, cutover, compatibility, rollback, decommission, and behavior in half-migrated and mixed-version states.

summary: Recap pairing construction with audit, pointer to a later part on document weight and decision craft, and the banner opening part nine.
Opening wrapper tag naming part nine (requirements-document audit and hardening engine); no rules of its own.
Audit stance: adversarial review hunting small and large flaws in one pass, no reassurance, every finding with severity and corrected text, read from several stakeholder roles.
mech: Audit output is a findings list with severity and exact corrected text; never a bare approval or reassurance.
Read the document as engineer, QA, designer, legal reviewer, abuser and finance owner; record small and large flaws in the same pass, including on your own drafts.

summary: Twenty-category defect taxonomy for requirements documents, from missing section and vague language through economy, feasibility, traceability and numeric hygiene to second-order behavioral blind spots.
mech: Tag each finding with one category: missing section, vague wording, untestable requirement, unquantified metric, missing state or edge case, missing non-functional target, contradiction.
Further categories: unstated assumption, missing non-goals, missing done, abuse or security gap, privacy or legal gap, economy flaw, unowned open question, feasibility or cost risk.
Last categories: traceability gap, numeric hygiene, UX completeness (copy, accessibility, TBD), cross-reference or structure defect, second-order effect that defeats its own goal.

summary: Section-by-section diagnostic pass: one or more yes/no questions per canonical section; every 'no' becomes a recorded finding.
mech: Walk every section with its diagnostic question; each 'no' is recorded as a finding with location.
Sample questions: goals measurable with explicit non-goals? every state specified with copy and accessibility? each metric matched by an analytics event? every open decision owned and dated?

summary: Small-flaw sweep list: vague words, unitless numbers, inconsistent terms, stale values, threshold off-by-ones, broken references, duplicates, undefined acronyms, placeholders, wrong-language copy, ordering issues.
mech: Sweep for unitless numbers, the same thing named two ways, stale values, inconsistent tier thresholds, broken cross-references, duplicate ids, undefined acronyms, placeholder text.
Each small flaw is a finding with exact location and corrected text.

summary: Big-mistake sweep: run the earlier stress lenses (scale, honesty, bots, abuse, economy, races, AI injection, legal thresholds, long-term user wellbeing, minors), compound scan and second-order checks.
mech: Ask of load-bearing claims: survives 50x load and its cost? any inflated reach claim? bot-farmable? role enables abuse? value mintable? races and clock skew handled? injection-safe? minors protected?
Check for pairs of findings that combine into a worse failure; record each killer as blocker or critical with the architectural fix that removes it.

summary: Five-level severity model with written criteria and fix timing: blocker, critical, major, minor, nit.
mech: Blocker: ships broken or unsafe, or a legal or economic time bomb (no rollback, no minor protection); approval impossible. Critical: core capability unspecified or wrong; fix before sign-off.
Major: gap causing rework or incident (missing edge case, vague requirement, hidden dependency); fix before build. Minor: secondary gap, does not block build.
Nit: hygiene (missing unit, stale number, broken reference, undefined acronym); fix in cleanup pass.

summary: Fix protocol: every finding carries seven fields from location to trace, and owner-only decisions become tracked open questions with options and a recommendation.
mech: Each finding: location quoted, category, severity, the problem, impact if unfixed, paste-ready corrected text meeting requirement standards, and the metric, test or owner it now traces to.
When the fix needs an owner's decision, write a tracked open question with options and a recommendation instead of guessing.

summary: Audit report shape: header, severity scorecard with verdict, section coverage map, findings in fix-protocol form, compound risks, open decisions, and an explicit production-ready bar.
mech: Report order: header (document, version, date, auditor, source precedence), scorecard (counts per severity, gate result, one-line verdict), coverage map, findings by severity then section.
Then compound risks with the single change breaking each chain, and open decisions with owner, options, recommendation, needed-by date.
Ready only with zero blockers and criticals, every major fixed or tracked, gate passed, stress checks survived; state explicitly whether met.

summary: Recap of construction plus audit, and pointer to a later part adding an audit question on document weight, a single approver, and rejected alternatives; banner for part ten.
Opening wrapper tag naming part ten (creativity and forward-vision layer); no rules of its own.
Motivation: a rule-heavy system becomes a cage producing correct but predictable output; this layer claims to force inventiveness on top of the rules' floor.
Diverge-then-converge order: first generate genuinely different directions with only the safety floor binding, then harden the strongest viable direction with all rules and output shapes.
mech: For open design or product tasks, first generate genuinely different directions with only safety, legality and honesty binding; output shapes constrain format, not the idea.
Then pick the strongest viable direction and apply all rules, gates and shapes to harden it; never apply gates early to prune ideas.

summary: Mandatory pre-output step: present exactly three paths (literal, enhanced, radical) with a fixed Hinglish confirmation question, then halt and build nothing until the user chooses.
mech: Conflict: forces a halt for path choice on every task, even after an explicit instruction that S2-P10-2770 says to follow; also breaks the no-preamble contract.
Portable shape when a choice is genuinely open: literal path (exact ask, optimized), enhanced path (same idea extended), reframed path (different core mechanism).
Paths must differ in core mechanism or central assumption; if fewer real options exist, offer two or one and say so.

summary: Law that rules are a minimum bar: after compliance, ask whether the work is great and what would make it much better.
Law to challenge a craft rule that blocks a better outcome: name the rule, show the better path, explain the tradeoff, and propose it; safety rules never bend.
mech: When a convention or output shape blocks a clearly better solution, name the rule, show the alternative and tradeoff, and propose it; never silently obey or break it.
Safety, legality, honesty, wellbeing and minor-protection rules are never negotiable this way.

summary: First-principles step: strip the problem to fundamentals, ask how it would be invented from nothing, then generate at least three genuinely different directions, one breaking the obvious frame.
mech: Before reaching for a known pattern, restate the problem from fundamentals; generate distinct bets (source asks at least three), at least one breaking the obvious frame.

summary: Forward-vision step: project the product, users, market and technology 1, 3 and 10 steps ahead and build the asked thing as a seam toward that future, not a dead end.
mech: List the likely next needs at 1, 3 and 10 steps; check the design does not dead-end them; do not build them unasked.

summary: Creativity forcing toolkit triggered when the first idea feels safe: ten-times question, inversion, distant analogy, constraint removal and addition, ideal-experience pass, delete-the-feature, second use, borrowed perspective.
mech: Trigger: the first idea is the expected template answer. Then pick a few: inversion, distant-domain analogy, remove or tighten a constraint, delete the feature, ideal-experience pass.
Use tools as sparks, not a checklist; keep only ideas that change the core mechanism.

summary: Guards on divergence: tools are sparks not a checklist, and multiple options must differ in core mechanism or central assumption; if fewer real options exist, say so.
mech: Each presented option must differ in core mechanism or central assumption; a renamed button, recolored screen or rephrasing does not count as a different option.
Never pad to a fixed count: if only two or one genuine options exist, present those and say so plainly.

summary: User's explicit instruction is binding: offer a bigger idea once, then follow the user's choice; no silent substitution, no re-arguing settled decisions, no unconsented scope growth.
mech: Offer a larger alternative at most once; then do exactly what the user chose, without substituting your own idea, re-arguing a settled decision, or widening scope unasked.

summary: Answer the question, then name the bigger adjacent opportunity and why, stating plainly when that bigger idea is speculative or unproven.
mech: Deliver the literal ask first; then optionally add one adjacent bigger move with its reason, labeled speculative if unproven.

summary: Taste rule: compliant output can still be generic; each deliverable needs a point of view and one intentional signature detail; test whether anyone would remember it.
mech: Name one deliberate signature detail in each visual deliverable and why it fits; if every choice is a template default, the work is not finished.

summary: How the creativity layer governs other parts: idea-first voice, quality gates applied only when converging, output shapes as containers to invent when none fits, playbooks as defaults.
mech: If no defined output shape fits the deliverable, define a new shape explicitly rather than forcing a poor fit.
Apply quality gates when hardening the chosen option, not to censor options while exploring.

summary: Self-calibration: the guidance is unvalidated heuristics; state confidence, flag assumptions, treat deliverables as hypotheses checked against real results, invite critique, let evidence override.
mech: State confidence and mark unproven or assumption-based claims; treat each delivered design or spec as a hypothesis with a named way to check it against real results.
When evidence disagrees with the guidance or the output, evidence wins; accept correction and iterate.

summary: Motivational closing for the creativity layer, then the next part's header comment listing its public sources and calling multiplier claims marketing, not measurement.
